title: Alon's 100-dominating directed graph problem
statement: Call a directed graph $D=(V,E)$ $s$-dominating if, for any subset $U$ of at most $s$ vertices of $V$, there is a vertex $v$ such that $(v,u)$ is a directed edge for every $u\in U$. Is it true that any 100-dominating finite directed graph contains a directed cycle of length at most 100?
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/01](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4791), page 70. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Seymour’s 1-flowing conjecture
statement: The 1-flowing conjecture predicts that the max-flow min-cut relation holds for all binary matroids that have no minor in $S := \{AG(3,2),T_{11},T_{11}^{*}\}$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2011/53](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/11451), page 28. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Lower bounds for linear-programming relaxations of constraint satisfaction problems
statement: For some constraint satisfaction problem, rule out that there exists a linear program of size polynomial in $n$ that achieves an approximation factor of $0.999$ for all instances on $n$ variables.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2012/54](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12177), page 18. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Conjectural structure of the unstable \[mathbb A^1\]-homotopy sheaf of a punctured affine space
statement:
Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic different from $2$. For every integer $n\ge 4$, there is an exact sequence of sheaves
\[
K^M_{n+2}/24\longrightarrow \pi^{\mathbb A^1}_n(\mathbb A^n\setminus 0)\longrightarrow GW^{n}_{n+1}.
\]
The sequence becomes short exact after $n$-fold contraction.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/32](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12495), page 32. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Improve the one-dimensional uniform-distribution discrepancy constant
statement: Let $c^*$ be the supremum of the constants $c$ such that, for every sequence $(x_n)_{n\ge 0}$ in $[0,1)$, the discrepancy satisfies $D_N \ge c\,\frac{\log N}{N}$ for infinitely many $N$. The report gives $0.06458\ldots \le c^* \le 0.222\ldots$. **Open Problem 2:** Improve this estimate for $c^*$, for example by the method indicated in the talk.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/49](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12723), page 35. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Serre’s uniformity problem for rational points on prime-level modular curves
statement: For every prime $p>37$, the rational points on each of the modular curves $X_0(p)$, $X_s^+(p)$, and $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^+(p)$ consist only of the cusps and the CM-points. Here the CM-points are the rational points arising from elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with complex multiplication, according as $p$ is ramified, split, or inert in the relevant endomorphism order.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/51](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12725), page 7. Canonicalized from 5 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Serre’s uniformity problem for the nonsplit Cartan modular curve
statement: For every prime number $p>37$, the rational points on the modular curve $X^+_{\mathrm{ns}}(p)$ consist only of the cusps and the CM-points.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2013/51](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/12725), page 8. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Generalized Bogomolov–Gieseker inequality for tilt-semistable objects on smooth projective threefolds
statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective threefold over $\a0\mathbb{C}$, and let $B,\omega\in\mathrm{NS}(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ with $\omega$ ample. For every tilt-semistable object $E\in\mathcal{B}_{\omega,B}$ satisfying $\nu_{\omega,B}(E)=0$, one has
$$\operatorname{ch}^{B}_{3}(E)\leq \frac{1}{18}\,\operatorname{ch}^{B}_{1}(E)\,\omega^{2}.$$
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2015/15](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13500), page 11. Canonicalized from 2 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Entropy minimization problem for incompressible viscous fluids
statement:
Let $X=\mathbb{T}^n$ and $\Omega=C([0,1],X)$. Let $R$ be the reversible Brownian path measure on $X$ with initial marginal $R_0=\mathrm{vol}$ and generator $\Delta/2$. Given a coupling $\pi\in\mathcal{P}(X^2)$ with $\pi_0=\pi_1=\mathrm{vol}$, minimize
\[
H(P\mid R)\quad\text{over }P\in\mathcal{P}(\Omega)\text{ such that }P_t=\mathrm{vol}\ \text{for all }0\le t\le1,\quad P_{01}=\pi.
\]
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2015/35](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13856), page 18. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Exact satisfiability threshold for random 4-SAT
statement: Conjecturally, the exact satisfiability threshold for random $4$-SAT is $m=9.93\ldots n$, where $n$ is the number of variables and $m$ is the number of independent uniformly random constraints.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2015/54](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/13949), page 25. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Existence of the dimension-24 sphere-packing auxiliary function
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2016/23](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14605), page 14. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Finiteness of level-1 algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of bounded motivic weight
statement: For every integer $N\ge 1$, there are only finitely many cuspidal automorphic representations $\pi$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, with $n$ varying, whose Artin conductor is $N$ and which are algebraic of motivic weight $\le 23$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2017/25](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/15433), page 14. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Willmore minimizers with prescribed isoperimetric ratio for spherical surfaces
statement:
For each prescribed isoperimetric ratio $\sigma\in(0,1]$, define
$$
\beta(\sigma)=\inf\left\{W(f): f:S^2\to\mathbb{R}^3\ \text{smooth immersed},\ I(f)=\sigma\right\},
$$
where
$$
W(f)=\frac14\int_{S^2}H^2\,d\mu_f,
\qquad
I(f)=\frac{\sqrt{36\pi}\,V(f)}{A(f)^{3/2}}.
$$
The report states that this infimum is attained by a smooth embedding of $S^2$ for every $\sigma\in(0,1]$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2017/35](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/15578), page 24. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Established properties of topological Hochschild homology
statement: Corollary 16 states that for every stable $\b5$-category $\b6C$, $\b6THH(C)=\b6THH(\operatorname{id}_C)$ carries a canonical $\b8T$-action. For every functor $F:\operatorname{Ind}C\to\operatorname{Ind}C$, the spectrum $\b6THH(F^p)\simeq\u0000b6THH(F,\ldots,F)$ carries a $\b6C_p$-action. Moreover, $\b6THH$ is Morita invariant and localizing.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2018/15](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/16156), page 60. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Coloring count cones for plane near-triangulations with a 5-cycle outer face
statement: For every plane near-triangulation $G$ with the outer face bounded by a 5-cycle, $n_G^\star$ is a non-negative linear combination of $n_{G_1},\ldots,n_{G_{11}}$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2019/1](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/16763), page 20. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Factorizable channels requiring infinite-dimensional ancillas
statement: For every integer $n\ge 11$, there exist factorizable Schur multipliers on $M_n(\mathbb C)$ that admit no finite-dimensional ancilla; indeed, they admit no type-I ancilla.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2019/37](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/17133), page 15. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Asymptotic count of $E_2$ almost primes in short intervals
statement:
Let $E_2$ denote the set of integers of the form $p_1p_2$, where $p_1,p_2$ are primes. For every fixed $\theta>0.55$, for sufficiently large $x$ and $H\\ge x^\theta$, one has
\[
\sum_{\substack{x<n\le x+H\\ n\in E_2}}1
=H\frac{\log\log x}{\log x}+O\!\left(H\frac{\log\log\log x}{\log x}\right).
\]
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2019/50](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/17293), page 38. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Banach’s geometric hypothesis in the exceptional case $n=133$
statement: Does every finite-dimensional real Banach space $V$ whose $133$-dimensional subspaces are all mutually isometric necessarily have an ellipsoidal unit ball, and hence be a Hilbert space? Equivalently, if all $133$-dimensional sections of the unit ball are affinely equivalent, must the unit ball be an ellipsoid?
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2020/30](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/1703876), page 26. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Bounded $H^\infty$-calculus for the degenerate boundary realization
statement: Under the setup on page 41, let $A_T$ be the $L^p$-realization of $A$ with boundary condition $T$. For every $0<\theta<\pi$, there exists a constant $\nu$ such that $A_T+\nu$ has a bounded $H^\infty$-calculus in $L^p(X)$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2021/27](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/7155448), page 41. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Non-polyhedrality of the effective cone of \(\overline{M}_{0,n}\)
statement: For every \(n\ge 10\), the effective cone \(\operatorname{Eff}(\overline{M}_{0,n})\) is not polyhedral in characteristic \(0\), and it is not polyhedral in characteristic \(p\) for an infinite set of primes \(p\) of positive density, including all primes \(p\le 2000\).
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2021/29](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/7155450), page 28. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Stabilization of the dimension of Teichmüller modular forms
statement: $\dim H^0(M_g,\lambda_g^{\otimes 12})=71$ for all $g\gg 0$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2021/6](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/4990375), page 21. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Inversion monotonicity for \b(231, 1324)-avoiding permutations
statement: For each fixed number of inversions $k$, the number of permutations of length $n$ in $\b(231,1324)$ having exactly $k$ inversions is weakly increasing as $n$ increases; equivalently, for all nonnegative integers $n$ and $k$, $$\left|\{\pi\in\operatorname{Av}_n(231,1324):\operatorname{inv}(\pi)=k\}\right|\leq\left|\{\pi\in\operatorname{Av}_{n+1}(231,1324):\operatorname{inv}(\pi)=k\}\right|.$$
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2024/6](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14298158), page 21. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Super-exponential anticoncentration for the permanent of a random Bernoulli matrix
statement: Can the exponential upper bound in Theorem 1 be improved to a super-exponential bound? More specifically, for a uniformly random $n\times n$ matrix $A_n$ with entries in $\{-1,1\}$, can the bound $\Pr[\operatorname{per}(A_n)=x]\le \exp(-cn)$, for every $x\in\mathbb R$ and some absolute constant $c>0$, be strengthened to a super-exponential bound, as conjectured by Vu [20, Conjecture 6.12]?
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2026/1](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299905), page 18. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Lower bound relating the window parameter to positional variance
statement: **Conjecture 10.** For every finite poset $P$ of size $n$ and every element $x\in P$, $\operatorname{win}(x)=\Omega\!\left(\frac{\sigma^2(x)}{n}\right)$, where $\sigma^2(x)=\operatorname{Var}(f(x))$.
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2026/1](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/14299905), page 34. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: London’s conjecture
statement: For every prime power $q$ such that $q\notin\{7,9,11,13\}$, let $n=q^{2}+q+1$. Among all $C_{4}$-free graphs $G$ on $n$ vertices with $\lvert E(G)\rvert=\frac{1}{2}q(q+1)^{2}$, one has $\tau(G)\le n^{(n-3)/2}$, with equality if and only if $G$ is an orthogonal polarity graph.
references: - [A Turán-type extremal problem for the number of spanning trees in C4-free graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34616) — arXiv — Shaohan Xu, Fengming Dong, Kexiang Xu

title: Green problem 45
statement: Can we pick residue classes $a_p \pmod{p}$, one for each prime $p \leq N$, such that every integer $\leq N$ lies in at least $10$ of them? Erdős remarks that he does not know how to answer it with $10$ replaced by $2$; this is `Erdos689.erdos_689`.

title: OEIS A185150 conjecture
statement:
Let $a(n)$ denote [OEIS A185150](https://oeis.org/A185150), with its indexing and defining sequence as given there.

Conjecture: $a(n) > 0$ for all $n > 0$. - _Zhi-Wei Sun_, Dec 29 2012

title: The converse as a conjecture
statement:
For an integer $n\ge 2$, let

$$
\binom{2n-1}{n-1}\equiv 1 \pmod{n^{k}}
$$

denote the congruence between the binomial coefficient
$\binom{2n-1}{n-1}$ and $1$ modulo $n^{k}$, where $k$ is a positive integer.

For every integer $n\ge 2$ such that

$$
\binom{2n-1}{n-1}\equiv 1 \pmod{n^{3}},
$$

the number $n$ is prime. Equivalently, no composite integer $n\ge
2$ satisfies $\binom{2n-1}{n-1}\equiv 1 \pmod{n^{3}}$.
references: 1. Wikipedia, [Wolstenholme's theorem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolstenholme%27s_theorem), the article this problem comes from.

title: Nonexistence conjecture for the half-power-sum congruence in the 1 modulo 4 case
statement:
Let $S_m(n)=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}j^m$. **Half-power-sum nonexistence conjecture.** For no odd positive integer $n\ge 5$ with $n\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ does

$$
S_{(n-1)/2}(n)\equiv 0\pmod{n^3}
$$

hold. The source proposes this after discussing related congruences and reports computational evidence through $n=20000$; no proof or counterexample is supplied.
source_name: Romeo Meštrović, “A congruence modulo n^3 involving two consecutive sums of powers and its applications”, arXiv:1211.4570 (2012).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.4570

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of November 2012). “Therefore, any counterexample to Giuga's conjecture must be squarefree.”

title: Hirsch's unbounded Hirsch conjecture
statement:
Let $Q$) denote a $(d+1)$-dimensional polyhedron with $n$ facets.

**Unbounded Hirsch conjecture.** The diameter of the $1$-skeleton of $Q$ is at most $n-(d+1)$.

The conjecture concerns the diameter bound proposed by Hirsch for arbitrary polyhedra. It was disproved by a counterexample of Klee and Walkup, so the unbounded version is refuted.
source_name: Karim Alexander Adiprasito and Bruno Benedetti, “The Hirsch conjecture holds for normal flag complexes”, arXiv:1303.3598 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1303.3598

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2013); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: The claimed equality $222+222=444$
statement:
Consider the displayed numerical equality. **Equality claim.** The following equality holds:

$$
222+222=444.
$$

This is an elementary arithmetic identity and is therefore solved.
source_name: Edward Tutaj, “Prime numbers with a certain extremal type property”, arXiv:1408.3609 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1408.3609

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of August 2014); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: Nonreducedness conjecture for invariant subspaces of nilpotent operators
statement:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space and let $T:V\to V$ be a nilpotent operator. Let $\mathcal{G}^T$ denote the scheme of subspaces invariant under $T$.

**Nonreducedness conjecture.** The scheme $\mathcal{G}^T$ is not reduced unless $T=0$.

The paper gives an explicit example exhibiting nonreducedness, but does not prove the assertion for every nonzero nilpotent operator.
source_name: Dinakar Muthiah, Alex Weekes and Oded Yacobi, “The equations defining affine Grassmannians in type A and a conjecture of Kreiman, Lakshmibai, Magyar, and Weyman”, arXiv:1708.06076 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.06076

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2017).

title: Wall's conjecture on maximal proper subgroups of finite groups
statement:
For a finite group $G$, let $\max(G)$ denote the number of maximal proper subgroups of $G$. **Wall's conjecture.**

$$
\max(G)\leq \lvert G\rvert.
$$

This conjecture concerns a uniform bound on maximal proper subgroups. The source notes that a counterexample was found during a 2012 AIM workshop, so the conjecture is refuted.
source_name: Keshab Chandra Bakshi, Sayan Das, Zhengwei Liu and Yunxiang Ren, “An angle between intermediate subfactors and its rigidity”, arXiv:1710.00285 (2017).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2017). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1610.07055](https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.07055).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.00285

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of October 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: Real Jacobian conjecture
statement:
Let $F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be a polynomial map. **Real Jacobian conjecture.** If

$$
\det F'(x)\ne 0\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb{R}^n,
$$

then $F$ is injective. The source explains that this real analogue is false: Pinchuk constructed a counterexample for $n=2$, so the conjecture is refuted.
source_name: Wei Liu and Quan Xu, “A minimax principle to the injectivity of the Jacobian conjecture”, arXiv:1902.03615 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.03615

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of February 2019); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

title: Tait's conjecture on Hamiltonian planar cubic graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a $3$-regular, $3$-connected planar graph. **Tait's conjecture.** Every such graph is Hamiltonian. The conjecture was disproved by W. T. Tutte, who constructed a counterexample on $46$ vertices; further counterexamples were found on $38$ vertices by Holton and McKay.
source_name: Saptarshi Bej, “Hamiltonian cycles in annular decomposable Barnette graphs”, arXiv:2008.06671 (2020).
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1712.06143](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.06143), [arXiv:1310.5504](https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.5504).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.06671

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of August 2020). “This conjecture was ultimately disproved by W.T. Tutte, when he constructed a couter-example to the conjecture, a graph built on $46$ vertices .”

title: Central binomial sum evaluation involving zeta values and powers of pi
statement:
Let

$$
S=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{\binom{2k}{k}}{2^{2k}(2k+1)^4}.
$$

**Central binomial sum conjecture.**

$$
S=\frac{1}{48}\left(6\pi\zeta(3)+4\pi\log^3 2+\pi^3\log 2\right).
$$

This identity is obtained by evaluating an arcsine logarithmic integral and was reported as having only computer verification in the source; its status therefore remains open.
source_name: Masato Kobayashi, “From Basel Problem to multiple zeta values”, arXiv:2112.03361 (2021).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:0911.2077](https://arxiv.org/abs/0911.2077).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03361

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2021).

title: James's conjecture for weight-5 blocks of Hecke algebras
statement:
Let $\hhh$ be a Hecke algebra and consider its blocks, with the weight of a block defined in the usual block-theoretic sense.

**James's conjecture.** James's conjecture holds for all weight $5$ blocks of $\hhh$.

The claim is based on computations made while searching for the paper's counterexample. The source gives no proof or independent resolution, so the conjecture remains open as stated.
source_name: Liron Speyer, “The minimal counterexample to James's conjecture”, arXiv:2601.08218 (2026).
references:
**6 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2006–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2310.08156](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08156), [arXiv:1909.07114](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.07114), [arXiv:1109.1489](https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.1489), [arXiv:0909.4844](https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.4844), [arXiv:math/0603314](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0603314).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08218

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2026). “To the astonishment of everyone in the field, Geordie Williamson disproved James's conjecture in .”

title: Artin's conjecture on forms over the $p$-adic numbers
statement:
For a field $k$, say that it is **$C_2$** if, for every form $F\in k[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ of degree $d$ with $n>d^2$, the equation

$$
F(X_1,\ldots,X_n)=0
$$

has a nontrivial solution in $k^n$. **Artin's conjecture.** For each prime number $p$, the field $\mathbb{Q}_p$ is $C_2$. The conjecture is false: Terjanian gave a counterexample in degree $d=4$ and $p=2$, later generalized to arbitrary $p$.
source_name: Sylvy Anscombe, “The model theory of perfectoid fields [after Jahnke and Kartas]”, arXiv:2602.23779 (2026).
references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2004–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2508.20192](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.20192), [arXiv:1002.3754](https://arxiv.org/abs/1002.3754), [arXiv:math/0410223](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0410223).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23779

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of February 2026). “The conjecture is false as shown by Terjanian's counterexample in degree $d=4$ and $p=2$, generalized to arbitrary $p$ later in .”

title: Exceptional packing coloring conjecture for claw-free subcubic graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a claw-free subcubic graph, and let $\mathcal{G}_{11}$ be the graph specified in the paper. **Exceptional packing coloring conjecture.** If $G\neq\mathcal{G}_{11}$, then $G$ is $(1,1,3,3,3)$-packing colorable. The paper exhibits $\mathcal{G}_{11}$ as a counterexample and conjectures that it is the unique exception; this classification remains open.
source_name: Ayman El Zein and Maidoun Mortada, “Impact of local girth on the S-packing coloring of k-saturated subcubic graphs”, arXiv:2603.25113 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.25113

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).

title: Harikae–Nakanishi–Uchida conjecture on $(2,2)$-move equivalence
statement:
A **link** is a link in $S^3$. Two links are **$(2,2)$-move equivalent** if one can be obtained from the other by finitely many $(2,2)$-moves and $(-2,-2)$-moves.

**Harikae–Nakanishi–Uchida conjecture.** Every link is $(2,2)$-move equivalent to a trivial link.

The conjecture was disproved: the knot $9_{49}$ is a counterexample, so the assertion does not hold as stated.
source_name: Mieczyslaw K. Dabkowski, Makiko Ishiwata and Jozef H. Przytycki, “Rational moves and tangle embeddings: (2,2)-moves as a case study”, arXiv:math/0501539 (2005).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0501539

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of January 2005). “Therefore, the Montesinos-Nakanishi conjecture does not hold.”

title: Existence of graphs outside the 2-OR-PCG class
statement:
A graph is a finite simple graph, and a **2-OR-PCG** is a graph in the 2-OR-PCG class, as defined in the paper.

**Existence conjecture.** There exist graphs that are not 2-OR-PCGs.

The paper notes that every graph with at most 10 vertices is a 2-OR-PCG, so any counterexample must have at least 11 vertices. The conjecture asserts that the 2-OR-PCG class is not the class of all graphs.
source_name: Tiziana Calamoneri, Manuel Lafond, Angelo Monti and Blerina Sinaimeri, “On Generalizations of Pairwise Compatibility Graphs”, arXiv:2112.08503 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.08503

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2021). “In Section we conclude proposing several open questions.”

title: Do Shannon capacity and its reversible variant coincide?
statement:
[2403.10985](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10985) introduced the notion of *reversible capacity* of a graph and showed that it is at most the Shannon capacity. It is conjectured there that the two values are equal.

At the finite-length level, it is known to fail: the maximum independent set of $C_7^3$ is strictly larger than the maximum *multirectangular* independent set (corresponding to reversible capacity sets). However, it remains possible that in the large-n limit they converge.
references: A. Meiburg, Bounding the Graph Capacity with Quantum Mechanics and Finite Automata, https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10985

title: Colin's problems (problem 1)
statement: Let $A$ be a graded algebra over a finite field satisfying Artin's conditions which is birationally PI, i.e. $Q_{\text{gr}}(A)_0$ is PI. Find "weak" conditions $(*)$ so that the deformations (i.e. the lifts to characteristic 0) are also birationally PI.
source_name: AimPL: Noncommutative surfaces and Artin's conjecture (posed by Colin Ingalls)

title: Analogous of paths on iterated monodromy groups for iterated Galois groups of dynamical maps
statement: 1. Can we algebraically construct "nice" paths to describe $G_\infty^{geom}$ by more explicit wreath recursions? More precisely, given $z\in f^{-1}(t)$, can we find explicit endomorphisms of $K_\infty$, perhaps recursively described, sending $t$ to $z$ with nice properties?
source_name: AimPL: Groups of dynamical origin (posed by Ophelia Adams)

title: Orbit equivalence for IMG
statement:
1. Can we find $\varphi \in Homeo(\partial T)$ such that the orbit of the group generated by $\varphi$ and $IMG(f)$ are orbit equivalent? 

2. Can we make $\varphi$ explicit?
source_name: AimPL: Groups of dynamical origin (posed by Constantine Medynets)

title: Maximal subgroups in Thompson groups
statement: Find new maximal subgroups of infinite index in Thompson groups

title: Describe the singularities of the smoothable component of … .
statement:
Describe the singularities of the smoothable component of ${\rm Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^n)$. To be more specific:

How large can the dimension of the Zariski tangent space to this component get?

Does the maximum occur in the intersection of components? Does it occur in the smoothable component?

title: Hilbert schemes of points (problem 3)
statement: What is the smallest $d$ such that ${\rm Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^3)$ is reducible?

title: Hilbert schemes of points (problem 4)
statement: Is there a nonreduced component of ${\rm Hilb}^d(\mathbb{A}^n)$? If so, find it.

title: What can we say about the set … ?
statement: What can we say about the set $Z^e$? Can we construct exotic components (i.e. components that only exist in characteristic $p$) using this stratification? Study the action by the Galois group ${\rm Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p/\mathbb{F}_p)$.
